title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Heading (partly illegible): 'Groupes loc. lib. en car. p (par réc. sur … p …)'. The most plausible reading is a programme for a crystalline Dieudonné description of finite locally free p-group schemes in characteristic p, done by recursion (presumably on the order).

(a) The data. M is a crystal of finite presentation on S_cris/Z_p. It is a perfect complex of amplitude in [-1,0], so locally a two-term complex of locally free crystals. It carries Frobenius and Verschiebung F_M : M^(p) -> M and V_M : M -> M^(p), with V∘F = p and F∘V = p. This is the natural derived replacement for a Dieudonné module of projective dimension 1. That is exactly what a finite flat group G = ker(G0 -> G1), with G0 and G1 Barsotti-Tate groups, should give: the cone of D(G1) -> D(G0).

Put Δ* = Lα*(M), where α : S_cris/F_p -> S_cris/Z_p. Then M ⊗L Z/p = Δ*, and (M^(p)) ⊗L Z/p = φ*(Δ*). Write M/F for cone(F) and M/V for cone(V). The octahedral axiom gives two exact triangles of complexes with F and V on S_cris/F_p:
- (I), from V∘F = p: M/F -> M^(p)/p = φ*Δ* -> M/V -> (M/F)[1].
- (II), from F∘V = p: M/V -> M/p = Δ* -> M/F ->.

(b) Descent. Triangle (I) is a 'filtration' on φ*(Δ*). Grothendieck wants to descend it via Frobenius to S_zar. The result is a triangle ℓ.[-1] --i0--> Δ* --π0--> ℓ̌. --∂0--> ℓ.[-1][1]. This is a derived Hodge filtration: ℓ is a co-Lie complex, ℓ̌ a Lie complex, and in the BT case one recovers ω_{G*} -> D(G)_S -> Lie(G).

(c) Deformation. Take a divided-power thickening S ⊂ S' (special case involving the ideal p·I_S). The crystal gives Δ*(S') = M ⊗L O_{S'}, which extends Δ*. One must then give an extension of the filtration, ℓ̄.[-1] -> Δ*(S') -> ℓ̌̄. This is the Grothendieck–Messing deformation recipe (lift the Hodge filtration) transposed to two-term complexes, i.e. to finite locally free group schemes rather than BT groups.

The neighbouring pages are unrelated: they come from a manuscript on base change for proper morphisms (H^1 and R^n f_*). This page belongs to the crystals / Barsotti–Tate circle of 1969–70.
errors: The triangles (I) and (II) are correct consequences of the octahedral axiom applied to V∘F = p and F∘V = p.

Gap: 'descending via φ' the filtration (I) on φ*(Δ*) to S_zar is not automatic. A sub-object of a Frobenius pull-back need not descend along Frobenius. In the BT case the Hodge filtration is defined independently and its Frobenius twist is the image of V. Here the descent is asserted as a programme step with no justification.

In characteristic p, with non-reduced or non-smooth S, it is now known that crystalline Dieudonné theory of finite flat groups is not an equivalence in general. Faithfulness and fullness need hypotheses (de Jong; Berthelot–Breen–Messing). So the implicit expectation of a classification is too optimistic without restrictions on S.

The deformation step is only sketched. No condition is given on which lifts of the filtration correspond to finite flat lifts. For truncated or finite groups the naive analogue of Grothendieck–Messing fails without extra data, cf. Illusie's treatment of truncated BT groups.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a programme to classify and deform finite locally free p-group schemes using Dieudonné crystals that are perfect complexes of amplitude [-1,0] with F,V. This includes a derived Hodge filtration obtained by Frobenius descent and a derived Grothendieck–Messing lifting criterion. The derived/complex formulation for finite flat groups was only realized decades later, in prismatic Dieudonné theory (Anschütz–Le Bras) and related work.
missed.quote: Cristal de prés. finie sur S_cris/Z_p d'amplitude parfaite ⊂ [-1,0], soit M, avec structures F_M et V_M … Descente à S_zar (via φ) de la "filtration" (I) … Prolongement à un épaississement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck already envisaged Dieudonné complexes (not modules) of amplitude [-1,0] as the right invariant of finite flat group schemes, together with a filtered deformation theory. This anticipates the derived viewpoint of modern prismatic Dieudonné theory. It is mainly of historical and attribution interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The general Grothendieck–Messing and crystalline Dieudonné programme is well known as his. What is less documented is the explicit derived formulation: amplitude-[-1,0] Dieudonné complexes for finite locally free groups, octahedral triangles for F and V, and a derived Hodge filtration with lifting along PD-thickenings. This anticipates later derived/prismatic treatments. The page is only a sketch, without results.
transcription_corrections: Heading likely 'Groupes loc. libres en car. p (par réc. sur … p …)', i.e. finite locally free group schemes in char p, defined by recursion; the exact recursion variable is illegible.
Top right: probably 'Δ* = Lα*(M)' (the definition given lower down), not 'Δ* = α*(Δ*)'.
Triangle (I): M⊗L/F --i_I--> M^(p)⊗L/p = φ*(Δ*) --π_I--> M⊗L/V --∂_I--> M⊗L/F[1]; the arrow ∂_I goes from M/V back to M/F.
Triangle (II): M⊗L/V -> M⊗L/p = Δ* -> M⊗L/F -> (M⊗L/V)[1]; the bottom label should read 'M⊗L/V', not '/∀'.
'p. div.' = 'à puissances divisées' (PD-thickening S' of S); the parenthetical reads roughly '(cas où S = Var(p·…))', i.e. a special case of the ideal of S in S'.
The last triangle should read ℓ̌̄. --∂̄0--> ℓ̄.[-1] --ī0--> Δ*(S') --π0--> ℓ̌̄., a lift of the filtration of b).
